column3: NASB moves “says this” to the end; “in the midst of” is rendered “among.”
NASB follows the critical text (“those who call themselves apostles”); “works” is rendered “deeds,” and “labor” “toil.”
NASB follows the critical text (“have endured … and have not grown weary”).
“Abandoned” is rendered “left”; NASB supplies “this.”
NASB follows the critical text, without “quickly”; “the first works” is rendered “the deeds you did at first.”
“Works” is rendered “deeds.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the Paradise of God”); “give” is rendered “grant.”
NASB moves “says this” to the end; “became dead” is rendered “was dead.”
NASB follows the critical text, without “your works”; it adds parentheses, and renders “slander” as “blasphemy.”
NASB follows the critical text (“is about to cast”); “unto death” is rendered “until death.”
“Injured” is rendered “hurt.”
NASB moves “says this” to the end.
NASB follows the critical text, without “your works” and “in which.”
NASB follows the critical text (“teaching Balak”); “a snare” is rendered “a stumbling block,” and NASB adds “acts of.”
NASB follows the critical text (“in the same way”).
NASB follows the critical text (“Therefore”); “lest then except” is rendered “or else.”
NASB follows the critical text, without “to eat”; it supplies “some of.”
NASB moves “says this” to the end.
NASB follows the critical text; “the latter” is rendered “of late,” and NASB supplies “at.”
NASB follows the critical text (without “a few things,” “you tolerate,” “she teaches and leads … astray”); “servants” is rendered “bond-servants.”
NASB follows the critical text (“she does not want to repent”).
NASB follows the critical text (“her deeds”); “sickbed” is rendered “a bed of sickness.”
“With death” is rendered “with pestilence,” and “affections” “minds.”
NASB follows the critical text; “deeps” is rendered “deep things,” and NASB supplies “them.”
“But” is rendered “Nevertheless.”
NASB puts the allusion in capitals; “works” is rendered “deeds.”
“Shepherd” is rendered “rule.” NASB ends this verse with “as I also have received authority from My Father,” which the Greek numbering places in verse 28, and supplies “authority.”
NASB begins the verse with “and I will give him the morning star”; the clause about the Father is in verse 27.
Close to the Greek.
